bibliography.title: Form Meets Function: Fiber Architecture Directs Proliferation and Differentiation in Gingival Keratinocytes
bibliography.authors: Ramminger I, Steinberg T, Rolauffs B, Selig M, Tomakidi P.

study.research_problem: Oral epithelial repair requires coordinated keratinocyte expansion and differentiation, but the way electrospun fiber orientation and diameter shape gingival-keratinocyte morphology, proliferation, differentiation, and basal-keratin dependence was incompletely defined.
study.exact_gap: Earlier topography studies typically examined limited fiber conditions and rarely linked cell/nuclear morphology, time-resolved proliferation, multi-stage differentiation markers, and KRT5/KRT14 perturbation in gingival keratinocytes (S002:C02-S002:C04).
study.objective_or_hypothesis: Test whether aligned versus random PCL fibers across three nominal diameter ranges produce distinct proliferative and differentiation-associated states and whether KRT5/KRT14 participate in the scaffold-dependent response (S002:C03-S002:C04).
study.study_design: Immortalized human gingival keratinocytes were cultured for 3 or 7 days on commercial aligned or random electrospun PCL mats and planar controls. Batch 1 contained three diameter ranges and supported characterization, morphometry, and ddPCR; batch 2 contained only the two smaller ranges and supported EdU, protein imaging, and siRNA/qPCR experiments (S003:C01-S003:C06).
study.sample_or_model: HPV16 E6/E7-immortalized human gingival keratinocytes at passages 38-49, commercial PCL mats from two production lots, generally three or four biological replicates; SEM cell imaging used one representative experiment per condition (S003:C01; S011:C01; S013:C02-S013:C03).
comparators: Nominal 600-800 nm, 1.2-1.7 micrometre, and 2.0-2.5 micrometre fiber ranges in batch 1
Only the two smaller diameter ranges in batch 2
KRT5 siRNA, KRT14 siRNA, and non-targeting siRNA within each recoverable surface condition
method_spine: Verify nominal fiber orientation and diameter by SEM while documenting proprietary fabrication and batch differences.
Quantify cell and nuclear morphology at two time points within each batch.
Measure cell density and EdU incorporation to distinguish accumulation from active S-phase entry.
Measure basal, early, and terminal differentiation-associated transcripts and proteins.
Perturb KRT5/KRT14 and examine recoverable RNA and downstream transcripts.
Separate observed architecture-response associations from unmeasured stiffness, mechanotransduction, viability, stratification, and regenerative function.

verification: SEM independently checked orientation and fiber-diameter ranges, but the example aligned small-fiber mean of 926 plus/minus 366 nm extends beyond the nominal 600-800-nm label and exact electrospinning parameters were proprietary (S003:C01-S003:C05).

Image-analysis workflows, RNA quality checks, non-targeting siRNA, and consistent acquisition settings support assay execution; ddPCR had no technical replicates because RNA was limited (S004:C01-S005:C02).
calibration: No mechanical or exposure calibration was performed. Morphometry pipelines were adapted from another cell type and manually queried, but no independent segmentation accuracy or inter-rater validation is reported (S005:C01).
validation: Directional orientation-related morphology trends recur in two commercial batches and gene/protein measurements provide partial orthogonal convergence, which is a robustness check rather than external biological validation (S014:C03-S014:C09; S018:C01-S019:C02).
The system was not validated in primary-cell, organotypic, barrier-function, animal, implant-interface, or clinical models.
sensitivity: Orientation, nominal diameter, time, and production batch are varied, but diameter is incomplete in batch 2 and orientation is entangled with fiber packing, thickness, and likely mechanics (S003:C03-S003:C05; S021:C05-S021:C07).
No stiffness, tensile, porosity, surface chemistry, degradation, seeding-density, calcium, or microbial/environmental sensitivity is tested.
application_prediction: A layered aligned-plus-random 'scaffold sandwich' for sequential proliferation and differentiation is a proposed design concept; the layered construct, stratification, barrier formation, and mucosal repair were not fabricated or tested (S021:C06-S022:C01).

primary_outcomes: Across batches, aligned fibers—especially the 1.2-1.7-micrometre range—produced more elongated cells and nuclei, whereas random fibers and controls produced rounder morphologies; absolute effect sizes differed between batches (S014:C01-S015:C05).

By day 7, aligned surfaces had higher cell densities and retained approximately 12-13% EdU-positive cells, while random and planar conditions fell below about 4% EdU despite some continued cell accumulation (S016:C01-S016:C03).

Random, particularly smaller-diameter, fibers showed higher basal and differentiation-associated transcript/protein signals; basal and suprabasal markers were simultaneously elevated and transcript/protein time trends did not always match (S017:C01-S018:C02).

After KRT5 or KRT14 knockdown, RNA from random-fiber conditions was near/below detection, preventing qPCR; aligned conditions retained RNA and showed context-dependent KRT1/KRT4/IVL/LMNB1/YAP1 transcript changes (S020:C01-S020:C05).
The two scaffold batches differed in diameter/configuration and absolute biological outcomes, but several orientation-dependent directions recurred (S019:C01-S019:C02; S021:C05).
study.highest_evidence_level_reached: Short-term in-vitro association and limited perturbation evidence in one immortalized gingival-keratinocyte system; no direct mechanics, viability after knockdown, organotypic tissue, animal, or regenerative-function validation.

argument_map.central_claim: Fiber orientation is associated with distinct short-term keratinocyte states—aligned mats with sustained proliferation and elongation, random mats with stronger differentiation-associated markers—and KRT5/KRT14 perturbation responses depend on topography; the data do not establish a complete mechanotransduction pathway, direct viability dependence, epithelial stratification, or mucosal-regeneration efficacy.
data: Two-batch cell/nuclear morphometry, cell density, EdU, ddPCR, marker-protein imaging, RNA yield, and siRNA/qPCR measurements (S014:C01-S020:C05).
SEM verifies approximate architecture but cell-seeded SEM is qualitative n=1 and contains preparation artifacts (S013:C01-S013:C03).
argument_map.warrant: Convergent geometry, proliferation, and marker patterns plus gene perturbation can support a topography-responsive cell-state model, while causal mechanics and tissue function require direct mechanical/exposure measurement, orthogonal viability, pathway localization/rescue, and tissue-level validation.
backing: The authors openly identify inter-batch differences and absence of tensile/stiffness testing, and treat the layered scaffold as future design work (S021:C05-S021:C08).
argument_map.qualifier: Within 3- to 7-day culture of HPV-immortalized gingival keratinocytes on two lots of thin commercial PCL mats.
rebuttals_or_boundaries: Batch 1 and batch 2 support different assays, so cross-assay biological chains also cross manufacturing lots and cannot be treated as one fully balanced factorial experiment.
The largest fiber range is absent from batch 2, preventing complete orientation-by-diameter replication for EdU, protein, and knockdown outcomes (S003:C04).
Orientation may covary with diameter distribution, cross-linking/packing, thickness, stiffness, elasticity, and transport, none of which is isolated (S003:C03-S003:C05; S021:C07).
RNA loss after knockdown was not confirmed by live/dead, apoptosis, cell counting, or rescue and therefore does not directly demonstrate viability collapse (S020:C03-S020:C05; S021:C04).
KRT/YAP/LMNB1 transcripts and morphology do not demonstrate force transmission, YAP nuclear translocation, nuclear integrity, chromatin change, or barrier differentiation.

measured: Fiber diameter/orientation by SEM; cell/nuclear shape descriptors; cell density; EdU fraction; KRT5/KRT14/KRT1/KRT10/KRT4/KRT13/IVL/FLG transcripts; selected protein fluorescence; RNA concentration; and post-siRNA transcript changes (S003:C01-S020:C05).
inferred: Filopodia-like protrusions are interpreted as integrin-rich focal adhesions without direct adhesion-protein localization or force measurement (S013:C03).
Lower day-7 EdU on random fibers is interpreted as cell-cycle exit and differentiation; EdU directly shows S-phase fraction but not the cause of decline (S016:C03).

Morphological/nuclear coupling is interpreted as cytoskeletal mechanotransduction and possible chromatin effects without mechanical characterization, traction, LINC, YAP localization, or chromatin assays (S015:C05; S021:C01-S021:C07).
Near-zero RNA after knockdown is interpreted as extensive cell loss and essentiality for viability without a direct viability assay or rescue (S020:C03-S020:C05).
Simultaneous basal and suprabasal marker expression is described as a transient differentiation state, but lineage/state resolution is not established (S021:C03).
Clustered EdU-positive cells are suggested to represent early epithelial self-assembly even though stratification was not quantified (S021:C02).
recommended: Use a balanced batch-crossed design with all diameters; quantify mat mechanics, porosity, thickness, and surface state; add primary cells, direct viability/rescue, YAP localization and force/pathway assays, organotypic stratification/barrier tests, and then evaluate the layered construct (S021:C05-S021:C08).
proxy_to_outcome_bridges: Cell elongation and nuclear shape are mechanosensitive readouts, not direct measurements of mechanical force or pathway activation.
EdU marks active DNA synthesis during a pulse, not long-term proliferative capacity or differentiation by itself.
Marker expression and co-expression do not establish a mature, stratified, functional oral epithelium.
RNA recovery is not a direct live/dead or apoptosis outcome.
A thin in-vitro electrospun membrane response does not establish peri-implant mucosal integration or regenerative efficacy.
overclaim_risks: The abstract/conclusion states that random-scaffold cells 'required' KRT5/KRT14 for viability, although viability was not directly assessed (S001:C01; S022:C01).
'Direct link' and 'programmable determinant' overstate a design with covarying architecture and unmeasured mechanics (S021:C03; S022:C01).
Calling aligned cultures basal/progenitor-like and random cultures differentiated simplifies simultaneous basal/suprabasal markers and incomplete functional endpoints.
The layered scaffold is a plausible hypothesis, not an experimentally demonstrated architecture (S021:C06-S022:C01).
Automated FE, animal, and porous-lattice cues are false; this is a short-term in-vitro electrospun-membrane study.

section_moves.move: Disclose batch-to-assay allocation and missing factorial cells
section_moves.execution: The paper states which assays used batch 1 or batch 2 and that the largest diameter was unavailable in batch 2 (S003:C04-S003:C05).
section_moves.transferable_principle: In biomaterial studies spanning manufacturing lots, map every assay to lot, factor level, sample size, and missing condition before integrating results across modalities.
section_moves.failure_mode: Directional replication across batches does not make an incomplete cross-batch factorial balanced.

section_moves.move: Separate population accumulation from active proliferation
section_moves.execution: Cell density and EdU fraction are reported together, allowing day-7 accumulation to coexist with low S-phase labeling on random fibers (S016:C01-S016:C03).
section_moves.transferable_principle: Pair cumulative cell number with a time-local proliferation assay and state what each measures before inferring cell-cycle exit or differentiation.
section_moves.failure_mode: Low EdU is not by itself proof of differentiation or loss of long-term growth potential.

section_moves.move: Use orthogonal levels while preserving discordance
section_moves.execution: The paper compares transcript and protein marker patterns and acknowledges that basal-marker time trends differ between modalities (S017:C01-S018:C02).
section_moves.transferable_principle: Build morphology-to-RNA-to-protein-to-perturbation chains, but report temporal or modal disagreement instead of calling every layer confirmatory.
section_moves.failure_mode: More assays do not establish a causal pathway when they use different batches and endpoints.

section_moves.move: Turn batch variation into a bounded robustness analysis
section_moves.execution: Absolute morphology and RNA outcomes differ between lots, while orientation-related directions are compared within batch and carried forward cautiously (S019:C01-S019:C02; S021:C05).
section_moves.transferable_principle: Normalize and interpret within manufacturing batch, report as-built differences, and call repeated direction a robustness signal rather than interchangeability.
section_moves.failure_mode: Do not pool materially different lots without a batch-aware model.

section_moves.move: Convert a complementary response pattern into a testable design hypothesis
section_moves.execution: Aligned-proliferative and random-differentiation signals motivate a proposed layered scaffold, with the actual construct left for future validation (S021:C06).
section_moves.transferable_principle: Write design translation as observation, design rule, proposed architecture, and discriminating validation experiment in separate sentences.
section_moves.failure_mode: A conceptual scaffold assembled from separate conditions is not a demonstrated regenerative device.

author_reported: Commercial fabrication parameters were proprietary; the two batches differed; the largest diameter was absent in batch 2; cell-seeded SEM was qualitative and affected by preparation artifacts; no tensile/stiffness testing was performed; YAP localization was not examined; viability after RNA loss was not directly measured (S003:C01-S003:C05; S013:C02-S013:C03; S020:C01; S021:C04-S021:C07).
reader_identified: A transformed, high-passage cell line and short 3/7-day culture limit physiological and translational inference.
Different batches and incomplete diameters support different modalities, confounding an integrated causal chain.
No measured porosity, permeability, mat thickness distribution, surface chemistry, stiffness, elasticity, tensile strength, or degradation.
Morphometry segmentation was adapted with manual acceptance but lacks reported detection accuracy/inter-rater reliability; different microscopes were used by batch.
Small n, many pairwise tests, and no clear factorial/repeated-time multiplicity model increase false-positive and interaction-interpretation risk (S011:C01).
No direct viability/apoptosis or rescue after knockdown, no YAP localization/traction force, no barrier/stratification function, and no primary/organotypic/in-vivo validation.
Random surfaces increase both basal and differentiation markers, complicating a single linear differentiation-state interpretation.
likely_bias_direction: Selective integration of cross-batch assays may exaggerate a coherent architecture-to-fate causal pathway.
RNA loss and morphology proxies likely overstate viability dependence and mechanotransduction certainty.
Regenerative-language framing overstates a short-term cell-state study.
limitations.scope_boundary: The study supports reproducible orientation-associated differences in short-term ihGK morphology, proliferation, and differentiation markers across two lots. It does not establish direct mechanical causation, KRT-dependent viability, mature epithelium, peri-implant integration, or mucosal regeneration.

writing_capability_candidates.capability: Write multi-batch biomaterial experiments with an assay-by-batch-by-factor map, reporting missing conditions and interpreting repeated directions separately from pooled effects.
writing_capability_candidates.manuscript_use: Methods, sample-flow diagram, Results robustness, and limitations.
writing_capability_candidates.counterexample_or_boundary: Two lots with different as-built structures and assay allocations do not form one balanced factorial dataset.

writing_capability_candidates.capability: Construct a morphology-to-proliferation-to-marker-to-perturbation evidence chain while tagging every link as measured, correlated, or mechanistically inferred.
writing_capability_candidates.manuscript_use: Results ordering, mechanobiology Discussion, and claim audit.
writing_capability_candidates.counterexample_or_boundary: Morphology, EdU, marker expression, and RNA loss do not directly measure force transmission, differentiation completion, or viability.

writing_capability_candidates.capability: Translate complementary in-vitro responses into a bounded device hypothesis by stating the proposed architecture and the unperformed validation sequence.
writing_capability_candidates.manuscript_use: Discussion design implications and future-work paragraph.
writing_capability_candidates.counterexample_or_boundary: A proposed aligned/random layered scaffold has not demonstrated stratification, barrier function, integration, or regeneration.

critical_weaknesses: Assays are split across structurally different batches and the largest diameter is not replicated.
Mechanical exposure, direct viability after knockdown, and key mechanotransduction endpoints are unmeasured.
Immortalized short-term culture and marker proxies do not validate regenerative function.

summary_zh: 这篇论文的价值在于展示一种多层证据链：纤维取向/直径—细胞和细胞核形态—EdU 与细胞密度—分化标志物—KRT5/KRT14 扰动。两批材料中，取向效应方向大体重复：aligned 更倾向持续增殖和伸长，random 更倾向较强的分化相关标志物。但各类实验分属不同批次，第二批缺少最大直径，且材料刚度、孔隙、厚度等未测，因此不能把取向直接当作唯一机械原因。尤其需要降格两类结论：敲低后 RNA 几乎消失并不是直接的细胞活性测量；形态和 YAP1 转录也不是机械转导或核转位证据。所谓 aligned/random 分层支架是一个值得验证的设计假说，而不是已经实现的口腔黏膜再生器械。
reader_notes: Primary Codex reader reviewed every non-reference packet section, including the complete batch-resolved Results and Discussion.
The finite-element, in-vivo-animal, and porous-lattice cues are false for this article.
The paper's unusually explicit batch disclosure is a strong writing model, while its viability and mechanotransduction wording supplies useful counterexamples.
